{{nihongo|'''Oyama Shrine'''|雄山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

{{List of coordinates}}
'''Oyama Shrine''' (おやまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Tateyama, Toyama|arz|تاتياما|ceb|Tateyama Machi|eo|Tatejamo|es|Tateyama (Toyama)|fa|توته‌یاما، تویاما|fr|Tateyama (Toyama)|id|Tateyama, Toyama|it|Tateyama (Toyama)|ja|立山町|ko|다테야마정|ms|Tateyama, Toyama|my|တတဲယာမမြို့၊ တိုယာမ|pl|Tateyama (Toyama)|ro|Tateyama, Toyama|ru|Татеяма (посёлок)|sv|Tateyama, Toyama|th|ทาเตยามะ (จังหวัดโทยามะ)|tl|Tateyama, Toyama|tr|Tateyama, Toyama|uk|Татеяма (Тояма)|ur|ٹاتیاما، تویاما|uz|Tateyama (Toyama)|zh|立山町|qid=Q670189}}, {{ill|Nakaniikawa District, Toyama|Q1204336|qid=Q1204336}}, {{ill|Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|qid=Q132929}}. Its former names were '''{{ill|Tateyama Gongen|Q11597837|qid=Q11597837}}''' and '''Oyama Gongen'''. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Etchū Province|ckb|پارێزگای ئێتچو|cs|Provincie Eččú|de|Provinz Etchū|es|Provincia de Etchū|fa|ولایت اتچو|fr|Province d'Etchū|gl|Provincia de Etchū|id|Provinsi Etchū|it|Etchū|ja|越中国|ko|엣추국|lt|Ečiū žemė|nl|Etchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Etchū|ru|Эттю (провинция)|simple|Etchū Province|sk|Eččú (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечу|tr|Etchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Еттю|vi|Tỉnh Etchū|zh|越中國|zh_min_nan|Ettyû-kok|zh_yue|越中國|qid=Q906899}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kokuhei-shōsha}}, and today it is a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ca|Associació de Santuaris Xinto|fr|Association des sanctuaires shinto|id|Asosiasi Kuil Shinto|it|Associazione dei santuari shintoisti|ja|神社本庁|ko|신사본청|ru|Дзиндзя хонтё|simple|Association of Shinto Shrines|sv|Jinja Honcho|zh|神社本廳|qid=Q908077}}.

=== Overview ===
With the sacred peak {{ill|Mount Tate|Q2977103|qid=Q2977103}} as its {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}, the shrine enshrines two deities as gods of Tateyama: {{ill|Izanagi|abstract|Q813858|ar|إزاناغي|az|İzanaqi|bcl|Izanagi|bn|ইজানাগি|bs|Izanagi|ca|Izanagi|cs|Izanagi a Izanami|da|Izanagi|el|Ιζανάγκι|eo|Izanagi|es|Izanagi|fa|ایزاناگی|fi|Izanaki|fr|Izanagi|he|איזאנגי|hr|Izanagi|hu|Izanagi|id|Izanagi|it|Izanagi|ja|イザナギ|ka|იძანაგი|ko|이자나기|lt|Idzanagis|mk|Изанаги|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯒꯤ|no|Izanagi|or|ଇଜାନାଗି|pt|Izanagi|ro|Izanagi|rsk|Изанаґи|ru|Идзанаги|simple|Izanagi|sk|Izanagi|sl|Izanagi|sr|Изанаки|sv|Izanagi|ta|இசநாகி|th|อิซานางิ|tl|Izanagi|tr|İzanagi|uk|Ідзанаґі|vi|Izanagi|zh|伊邪那岐|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Ōkami}} (Tateyama Gongen Oyama no Kami, whose Buddhist honji is {{ill|Amitābha|Q236242|qid=Q236242}}) and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Kami}} (Tachio Tenjin Tsurugi-dake no Kami, whose honji is {{ill|Acala|Q337624|qid=Q337624}}). During the era of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}, it was a shrine with strong Buddhist elements and became the source of {{ill|Tateyama Shugen|Q11597829|qid=Q11597829}}. It also served as an imperial prayer site for {{ill|Empress Genmei|Q233224|qid=Q233224}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Daigo|Q313942|qid=Q313942}}.

The shrine consists of three sanctuaries: '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mine-honsha}}''' (みねほんしゃ), '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chūgū Kiganden}}''' (ちゅうぐうきがんでん), and '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Maedate Shadan}}''' (まえだてしゃだん). These collectively are known as Oyama Shrine. They are located across a wide area from {{ill|Ashikuraji|Q11614856|qid=Q11614856}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Toyama|arz|تاتياما|ceb|Tateyama Machi|eo|Tatejamo|es|Tateyama (Toyama)|fa|توته‌یاما، تویاما|fr|Tateyama (Toyama)|id|Tateyama, Toyama|it|Tateyama (Toyama)|ja|立山町|ko|다테야마정|ms|Tateyama, Toyama|my|တတဲယာမမြို့၊ တိုယာမ|pl|Tateyama (Toyama)|ro|Tateyama, Toyama|ru|Татеяма (посёлок)|sv|Tateyama, Toyama|th|ทาเตยามะ (จังหวัดโทยามะ)|tl|Tateyama, Toyama|tr|Tateyama, Toyama|uk|Татеяма (Тояма)|ur|ٹاتیاما، تویاما|uz|Tateyama (Toyama)|zh|立山町|qid=Q670189}} to Iwakuraji, broadly encompassing the entire Tateyama mountain range including Jigokudani and Midagahara.

There is also a small Oyama Shrine, a subsidiary of Tateyama, in {{ill|Kamiichi, Toyama|Q1204302|qid=Q1204302}}{{ill|新屋|Q11501967|qid=Q11501967}}.

The character “'''峅'''” used in Iwakuraji and Ashikuraji is said to mean “a place where the gods descend.”

It is said that worship at any of the three shrines—Mine-honsha, Chūgū Kiganden, or Maedate Shadan—brings the same blessings. This is because Mine-honsha at the summit can only be visited from the 7th to 9th months of the lunar calendar; Chūgū Kiganden faces the main peak Oyama and is where the founder spent his later years; and Maedate Shadan is where the legend of the opening of Tateyama begins. In addition, it is said that in the past the {{ill|Gūji|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500}} walked from Maedate Shadan in Iwakuraji up to Mine-honsha at the summit, and even today the chief priest of Maedate Shadan also serves as the chief priest of Mine-honsha.

The current enshrined deities are the following two:
* '''{{ill|Izanagi|abstract|Q813858|ar|إزاناغي|az|İzanaqi|bcl|Izanagi|bn|ইজানাগি|bs|Izanagi|ca|Izanagi|cs|Izanagi a Izanami|da|Izanagi|el|Ιζανάγκι|eo|Izanagi|es|Izanagi|fa|ایزاناگی|fi|Izanaki|fr|Izanagi|he|איזאנגי|hr|Izanagi|hu|Izanagi|id|Izanagi|it|Izanagi|ja|イザナギ|ka|იძანაგი|ko|이자나기|lt|Idzanagis|mk|Изанаги|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯒꯤ|no|Izanagi|or|ଇଜାନାଗି|pt|Izanagi|ro|Izanagi|rsk|Изанаґи|ru|Идзанаги|simple|Izanagi|sk|Izanagi|sl|Izanagi|sr|Изанаки|sv|Izanagi|ta|இசநாகி|th|อิซานางิ|tl|Izanagi|tr|İzanagi|uk|Ідзанаґі|vi|Izanagi|zh|伊邪那岐|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Ōkami}}''' (いざなぎのかみ)
* '''{{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|fr|Tajikarao|it|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|アメノタヂカラオ|ko|아메노타지카라오|ru|Амэ-но Тадзикарао|simple|Ame-no-Tajikarao|zh|天手力男神|qid=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Kami}}''' (あめのたぢからおのかみ)

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown. According to shrine tradition, in the first year of {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taihō}} ({{ill|701|Q23496|qid=Q23496}}), {{ill|Saeki no Ariyori|ja|佐伯有頼|qid=Q11382848}}, the son of Saeki no Sukune Ariwaka, a provincial governor of {{ill|Etchū Province|ckb|پارێزگای ئێتچو|cs|Provincie Eččú|de|Provinz Etchū|es|Provincia de Etchū|fa|ولایت اتچو|fr|Province d'Etchū|gl|Provincia de Etchū|id|Provinsi Etchū|it|Etchū|ja|越中国|ko|엣추국|lt|Ečiū žemė|nl|Etchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Etchū|ru|Эттю (провинция)|simple|Etchū Province|sk|Eččú (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечу|tr|Etchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Еттю|vi|Tỉnh Etchū|zh|越中國|zh_min_nan|Ettyû-kok|zh_yue|越中國|qid=Q906899}} said to be a descendant of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}}, was guided by a white hawk to a cave. There he received a divine oracle from Oyama Ōkami stating: “I appear on this mountain to save sentient beings of the defiled world. Sometimes I take the form of a {{ill|Hawk|Q846664|qid=Q846664}}, sometimes that of a {{ill|Bear|Q11788|qid=Q11788}}. I have guided you here so that you may open this sacred mountain.” Based on this oracle, the sacred mountain was opened and developed. It is also said that in the third year of Taihō ({{ill|703|Q23500|qid=Q23500}}), Shakyō Kyōkō enshrined the deity.

Volume 17 of the {{ill|Man'yōshū|ar|مان يوشو|az|Manyoşu|be|Ман’ёсю|ca|Man'yōshū|cs|Manjóšú|de|Man’yōshū|eo|Man'joŝu|es|Man'yōshū|fa|مان‌یوشو|fi|Man’yōshū|fr|Man'yōshū|hi|मानयोशू|hr|Man'yōshū|hu|Manjósú|id|Manyōshū|it|Man'yōshū|ja|万葉集|ko|만엽집|la|Man'yōshū|mr|मान्योशू|nl|Man'yōshū|pl|Man’yōshū|pt|Man'yōshū|ru|Манъёсю|sh|Man'yōshū|simple|Man'yōshū|sk|Manjóšú|sv|Manyoshu|tl|Man'yōshū|tr|Man'yōshū|uk|Манйосю|uz|Manyoshyu|vi|Vạn diệp tập|wuu|萬葉集|zh|萬葉集|zh_classical|萬葉集|zh_min_nan|Bān-ia̍p-chi̍p|zh_yue|萬葉集|qid=Q834321}} includes the “Ode to Tateyama,” composed on April 27 in {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 18 ({{ill|746|Q23616|qid=Q23616}}) by {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|qid=Q386308}}, who was then the provincial governor of Etchū.

According to official histories, the shrine received promotions in {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} on two occasions:
* {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}: Entry for September 25, {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 5 ({{ill|863|Q25052|qid=Q25052}}), promoted from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade}} to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade}} by {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243}}.
* {{ill|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542|qid=Q1053542}}: Entry for August 22, {{ill|Kanpyō (era)|Q1346292|qid=Q1346292}} 1 ({{ill|889|Q23833|qid=Q23833}}), promoted from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade}} to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} by {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267}}.

In {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), it was listed as a minor shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}. According to *{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=The Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places – Vol. 8 Hokuriku}}*, texts such as the *Shintōshū* by Angyō-in from the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}} and *Nihon Kanoko* describe it as the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Etchū Province|ckb|پارێزگای ئێتچو|cs|Provincie Eččú|de|Provinz Etchū|es|Provincia de Etchū|fa|ولایت اتچو|fr|Province d'Etchū|gl|Provincia de Etchū|id|Provinsi Etchū|it|Etchū|ja|越中国|ko|엣추국|lt|Ečiū žemė|nl|Etchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Etchū|ru|Эттю (провинция)|simple|Etchū Province|sk|Eččú (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечу|tr|Etchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Еттю|vi|Tỉnh Etchū|zh|越中國|zh_min_nan|Ettyû-kok|zh_yue|越中國|qid=Q906899}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it became a prefectural shrine, and in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 15 ({{ill|1940|Q18633|qid=Q18633}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kokuhei-shōsha}}. After World War II, it became a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ca|Associació de Santuaris Xinto|fr|Association des sanctuaires shinto|id|Asosiasi Kuil Shinto|it|Associazione dei santuari shintoisti|ja|神社本庁|ko|신사본청|ru|Дзиндзя хонтё|simple|Association of Shinto Shrines|sv|Jinja Honcho|zh|神社本廳|qid=Q908077}}.

Since ancient times, Tateyama has been revered nationwide as one of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Three Sacred Mountains}} alongside {{ill|Mount Fuji|Q39231|qid=Q39231}} and {{ill|Mount Haku|Q2639098|qid=Q2639098}}. Today it is often called “Tateyama climbing” as a tourist or sporting activity, but originally it was “Tateyama worship,” undertaken for the purpose of pilgrimage.

=== Grounds ===
=== Mine-honsha ===
{{Shinto shrine
|Name = Oyama Shrine Mine-honsha
|Image = [[File:Mine-honsha.JPG|250px|Mine-honsha]]<br />Mine-honsha, shrine building and torii (distant view)
|Location = 1 Tateyama Mine, Tateyama Town, Nakaniikawa District, Toyama Prefecture (summit of Mount Oyama)
|Coordinates = {{Wikicoord|36|34|23.44|N|137|37|4.51|E|region:JP-16|name=Oyama Shrine Mine-honsha}}
|Deities =

|Founded =
|Main hall =
|Other names =
|Annual festival = {{ill|July 25|Q2720|qid=Q2720}}
|Rituals =

==== Overview ====
Until {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Man’en}} 1 ({{ill|1860|Q7691|qid=Q7691}}), successive lords of the {{ill|Kaga Domain|fa|قلمرو کاگا|fr|Domaine de Kaga|ja|加賀藩|ko|가가번|ru|Кага (княжество)|wuu|加贺藩|zh|加賀藩|qid=Q903448}} from the {{ill|Maeda clan|Q578033|qid=Q578033}} constructed the shrine buildings. After the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} period, construction ceased for some time, but in July of {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 8 ({{ill|1996|Q2070|qid=Q2070}}), the shrine building was rebuilt for the first time in 136 years. Mine-honsha is located at the summit of Mount Oyama (3,003 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m}}), and winter worship is impossible, so Maedate Shadan was built at the mountain’s foot in Iwakuraji to conduct rituals year-round.

According to *Toyama Prefectural History: Folklore Volume*, in village communities before World War II—particularly in {{ill|Niikawa district|ja|新川郡|zh|新川郡|qid=Q11502110}}—it was customary for local youths to undertake the Tateyama pilgrimage as a rite of passage by age 15 at the earliest, or by age 18 at the latest upon coming of age ({{ill|Genpuku|Q138321|qid=Q138321}}). Those who did not make the pilgrimage were sometimes subject to social criticism. However, since the pilgrimage required a month of abstaining from killing and observing ritual purity beforehand, as well as postponement in cases of mourning, there were instances where it was not undertaken. Pilgrims prepared entirely new white garments, never reusing even a younger brother’s clothing, and even their walking staff was newly made. Around {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}, clothing colors and styles became freer, but before that, white attire was the norm. This custom has been passed down through school climbing activities, and even as of {{ill|2009|Q1996|qid=Q1996}}, some elementary schools in Toyama Prefecture still include Tateyama climbing as an annual event.

Pilgrims would pick up one to three stones along riverbeds on the way and offer them beside Mine-honsha, laying them in the forecourt. According to local tradition recorded in *Toyama Prefectural History: Folklore Volume*, this practice stemmed from a tale that when Tateyama and {{ill|Mount Haku|Q2639098|qid=Q2639098}} in {{ill|Kaga Province|Q907469|qid=Q907469|lt=Kaga}} compared heights, Tateyama was lower by the thickness of a horse’s straw sandal, so stones were carried up to make it taller. The same source also considers other examples—such as the {{ill|Oshiraishimochi|Q17225061|qid=Q17225061}} at {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}, the river stones laid in the sacred court of Ashikuraji Wakamiya ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chūgū Kiganden}}), and the offering of three clean beach stones called “Okesoku” at graves during {{ill|Obon|ar|مهرجان الأوبون|az|Bon festivalı|ca|Obon|da|Obon|de|Obon|el|Ομπόν|eo|Obon|es|O-bon|fa|اوبون (جشن)|fi|Obon|fr|O bon|gd|O-bon|he|אובון|hi|बॉन त्योहार|hu|Obon|id|Obon|it|Bon Festival|ja|お盆|ko|오본|lt|Obon festivalis|ms|Bon (perayaan)|my|ဘွန်းပွဲတော်|nl|Obon (festival)|nn|O-bon|pl|O-bon|ro|Festivalul Bon|ru|Обон (праздник)|sr|Бон Фестивал|th|เทศกาลบง|tr|Bon Festivali|uk|О-бон|vi|Lễ hội Bon|zh|御盆|qid=Q1154888}} in {{ill|Asahi, Toyama|Q1204470|qid=Q1204470}}—and suggests that, while differing from ancestor worship, the stones may have been offerings imbued with divine or magical power to the god of Tateyama.

According to *Toyama Prefectural History: Folklore Volume*, pilgrims would buy red long banners as souvenirs when descending the mountain, or descend with such banners raised. As of {{ill|2009|Q1996|qid=Q1996}}, pilgrims who receive prayers for safe climbing in front of the Mine-honsha shrine building are given a red talisman reading “Oyama Shrine at the Summit of Tateyama,” which they attach to white wooden kongō staffs, trekking poles, or {{ill|Backpack|Q5843|qid=Q5843}} while descending.

=== Chūgū Prayer Hall ===
{{Shrine
|Name        = Oyama Shrine Chūgū Prayer Hall

{{main|Ashikuraji}}
==== Overview ====
The Chūgū Prayer Hall is a syncretic Shinto-Buddhist ({{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}) facility formerly known as **Chūgū-ji Temple** (Ashikuraji). It serves as the center of Tateyama worship at Ashikuraji. Positioned directly facing the main peak of Mount Tateyama, “Oyama,” the founder {{ill|Saeki no Ariyori|ja|佐伯有頼|qid=Q11382848}} spent his later years at this site.

Since ancient times it has enjoyed deep devotion from warriors and court nobles, who dedicated offerings to “Oba-sama.” The surrounding area contains temple lodgings and structures such as the Nunobashi Bridge, used for rites of salvation for women. Within the Tateyama faith, which traditionally prohibited women from entering sacred areas, this was the final point women were permitted to access.

The followers of Ashikuraji formed a unique organization called the “Ichizankai.” From the {{ill|16th century|Q7017|qid=Q7017}} onward, they traveled throughout the provinces distributing talismans, Tateyama origin scrolls, Tateyama Gyūō paper charms, as well as medicinal herbs and powders, collecting payment the following year. This organization is also regarded as the origin of Toyama’s traveling medicine trade.

At the rear of the precincts stand the West Main Hall (Tateyama Ōmiya) and the East Main Hall (Tateyama Wakamiya). The “Prayer Hall” was formerly known as the Great Lecture Hall until the Edo period, and enshrines Oyama Ōkami together with the deities of 36 shrines located throughout Mount Tateyama.

* West Main Hall (Tateyama Ōmiya) — Enshrined deities: Tateyama Gongen Izanagi Ōkami; subsidiary deities Emperor Monmu and Saeki Sukune Ariwaka
* East Main Hall (Tateyama Wakamiya) — Enshrined deities: Tachi-o Tenjin (Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto), Inase Irihiko-no-Mikoto, and Saeki no Ariyori-no-Mikoto
* Auxiliary Shrine (Tateyama Kaisandō) — Enshrined deity: Saeki no Ariyori
* Subsidiary and branch shrines: Hōdō Shrine, Shinmei Shrine, Suijin Shrine, Akai-ike Shrine, Inari Shrine, Shinpi Shrine (Yamagami Shrine)
* Other facilities: Tateyama Kaisan Mausoleum, Stone Dance Stage, Saikai Bridge
* Historical documents: 56 bound volumes and 328 additional items

Adjacent to the site is the Tateyama Faith–themed {{ill|Theme park|Q2416723|qid=Q2416723}}, the Prefectural {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tateyama Museum}}.

* Access: From {{ill|Chigaki Station|Q5097198|qid=Q5097198}} on the {{ill|Toyama Chihō Railway Tateyama Line|Q7830575|qid=Q7830575}}, take the Tateyama Town bus for 5 minutes and get off at the Ashikuraji bus stop (no service on Sundays).

==== Overview ====
The Maedate Shrine Platform is a syncretic Shinto-Buddhist ({{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}) site that originated from Tateyama-dera Temple (Iwakuraji), founded in the early Heian period. It served as the center of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tateyama worship}} at Iwakuraji.

The site stands directly in front of a cave where the founder {{ill|Saeki no Ariyori|ja|佐伯有頼|qid=Q11382848}} was guided by a white hawk, a manifestation of {{ill|Tateyama Gongen|Q11597837|qid=Q11597837}}, marking the beginning of the legend of Tateyama’s sacred opening. Revered by warriors and court nobles alike, offerings to Tateyama Gongen were traditionally dedicated here.

Those entering {{ill|Mount Tate|Q2977103|qid=Q2977103}} purified bodily defilement and sins through hot-water purification rites and prayed for safety along the journey. Even today, temple lodgings, old mountain trails, and stone Buddhas remain scattered nearby. Tateyama mandalas are still preserved in the lodgings, which once spread Tateyama worship to followers nationwide.

Beside the site flows the {{ill|Jōganji River|Q994562|qid=Q994562}}, known as Japan’s most violent river ({{ill|raging river|Q11514995|qid=Q11514995}}). Repeated flood damage reduced the complex to its present scale, but numerous shrines downstream enshrine sacred objects said to have been carried away from this site, suggesting that it was once far larger.

The buildings originally constructed by {{ill|Saeki no Ariyori|ja|佐伯有頼|qid=Q11382848}} survive only in ancient documents. The present structures were restored and rebuilt by {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ar|ميناموتو نو يوريتومو|be|Мінамота-но Ёрытома|bg|Минамото но Йоритомо|br|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ca|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ckb|مینامۆتۆ نۆ یۆریتۆمۆ|cs|Joritomo Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoritomo|el|Μιναμότο νο Γιοριτόμο|eo|Minamoto no Yoritomo|es|Minamoto no Yoritomo|eu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fa|میناموتو نو یوریتومو|fi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|hak|Minamoto no Yoritomo|he|מינאמוטו נו יוריטומו|hu|Minamoto no Joritomo|id|Minamoto no Yoritomo|it|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|ko|미나모토노 요리토모|la|Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt|Minamoto no Joritomo|mr|मिनामोटो नो योरिमोटो|ms|Minamoto no Yoritomo|nl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|pl|Yoritomo Minamoto|pt|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ro|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ru|Минамото-но Ёритомо|sh|Minamoto no Yoritomo|sk|Joritomo Minamoto|sl|Minamoto no Joritomo|sq|Minamoto no Joritomo|sr|Минамото но Јоритомо|sv|Minamoto no Yoritomo|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยริโตโมะ|tl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|tr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|uk|Мінамото-но Йорітомо|vi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|war|Minamoto no Yoritomo|wuu|源赖朝|zh|源赖朝|zh_min_nan|Minamoto no Yoritomo|zh_yue|源賴朝|zu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800}} and later repaired by {{ill|Lanuvio|Q242793|qid=Q242793}}. As a result, it is a rare shrine whose buildings do not bear the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chrysanthemum Crest}}.

Because it stands at the entrance to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tateyama worship}}, the shrine is characterized by having torii gates (front torii and east torii) and shrine gates (front shrine gate and east shrine gate) on both sides of the main hall.

* Main hall architectural style: Nagare-zukuri with a five-bay frontage and one-bay porch, roofed with cypress bark (the largest main hall of its type in Hokuriku)
* Subsidiary and branch shrines: Inari Shrine, Tachi-o Shrine, Hachiman Shrine
* Former subsidiary structures: Great Lecture Hall, Goma Hall, Worship Hall, Hōrin Hall, Suijin Shrine, Inari Hall, Aizen Shrine, Kannon Hall, Jizō Hall, Wakamiya Shrine Hall, and others
* Other facilities: Monument inscribed with Emperor {{ill|Hirohito|Q34479|qid=Q34479}}’s poem “{{ill|Tateyama no Uta|Q21015447|qid=Q21015447}},” former Saikan Hall
* Historical documents: 481 items
* Access: About 10 minutes on foot from {{ill|Iwakuraji Station|ja|岩峅寺駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iwakuraji|ko|이와쿠라지역|my|အိဝခုရဂျိဘူတာ|ur|ایواکوراجی اسٹیشن|zh|岩峅寺車站|qid=Q6100451}} on the {{ill|Toyama Chihō Railway Tateyama Line|Q7830575|qid=Q7830575}}, or about 15 minutes on foot from {{ill|Daisenji Station|ja|大川寺駅|jv|Setatsiyun Daisenji|ko|다이센지역|my|ဒိုင်းဆင်းဂျိဘူတာ|ur|دائیسینجی اسٹیشن|zh|大川寺站|qid=Q5209603}} on the {{ill|Toyama Chihō Railway Kamidaki Line|fr|Ligne Kamidaki|ja|富山地方鉄道上滝線|ko|도야마 지방 철도 가미다키선|zh|上瀧線|qid=Q7830572}}

=== Festivals and Rituals ===
* January 1 – New Year’s Day Festival
* January 2 – Beginning of Daily Offerings Festival
* January 3 – {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|qid=Q11387821}}
* April 8 – Spring Grand Festival, Mikoshi Procession
* April 29 – Emperor Shōwa Festival
* Auspicious day in June – Prayer for Bountiful Harvest
* June 30 – {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|fa|اوهارائه‌شیکی|fr|Ōharae-shiki|ja|大祓|ko|오하라에|simple|Ōharae-shiki|qid=Q11261910|lt=Summer Purification Rite}}
* July 7 – Industry and Traffic Safety Prayer Festival
* July 25 – Mine Main Shrine Festival
* August 21 – Branch Inari Shrine Festival
* August 25 – Branch Hachiman Shrine Festival
* September 15 – Subsidiary Tachi-o Shrine Festival
* November 3 – Autumn Grand Festival ({{ill|Chigo Dance of Etchū|Q11636372|qid=Q11636372|lt=Chigo Dance}}; Tateyama no Mai ({{ill|miko mai|Q11479841|qid=Q11479841}}))
* Auspicious day in November – New Grain Thanksgiving Festival
* December 23 – {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenchō-sai}}
* December 31 – Year-End Purification Rite
* December 31 – New Year’s Eve Festival
* Monthly on the 1st – Monthly Festival and Traffic Safety Prayer Festival

=== Cultural Properties ===
=== Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) ===
* Maedate Shrine Platform Main Hall
* Wooden Seated Statue of Monk Jikō

=== Other Items ===
* Autographed manuscript by Emperor Go-Kōmyō
* Folding fan of Emperor Nakamikado
* Crown of Emperor Sakuramachi
* Stone komainu guardian lions
* Boiling cauldron used in divination rites
* Tateyama Mandala paintings
* And many others

=== Transportation Access ===
; Mine Main Shrine
* About a 2-hour mountain climb from {{ill|Murodō Station|Q6938821|qid=Q6938821}} on the {{ill|Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route|Q6425988|qid=Q6425988}}

; Chūgū Prayer Hall
* From {{ill|Chigaki Station|Q5097198|qid=Q5097198}} on the {{ill|Toyama Chihō Railway Tateyama Line|Q7830575|qid=Q7830575|lt=Tateyama Line}}, take the Tateyama Town bus (bound for Ashikuraji) and get off at “Oyama Shrine-mae”

; Maedate Shrine Platform
* About a 7-minute walk from {{ill|Iwakuraji Station|ja|岩峅寺駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iwakuraji|ko|이와쿠라지역|my|အိဝခုရဂျိဘူတာ|ur|ایواکوراجی اسٹیشن|zh|岩峅寺車站|qid=Q6100451}} on the {{ill|Toyama Chihō Railway Tateyama Line|Q7830575|qid=Q7830575|lt=Tateyama Line}} and {{ill|Toyama Chihō Railway Kamidaki Line|fr|Ligne Kamidaki|ja|富山地方鉄道上滝線|ko|도야마 지방 철도 가미다키선|zh|上瀧線|qid=Q7830572|lt=Kamitaki Line}}
